T: Drive the cattle north. Eat like a drover.
D: An English aristocrat and a rough drover take a herd of cattle across northern Australia on the eve of war.
P: Serve the mains when the drive makes camp for the night.
S: the cattle drive across the Top End
Self-raising flour with butter rubbed in, milk mixed in with a knife, shaped into a round, scored, baked at 200C for 30 minutes, with butter and golden syrup.
the ball in Darwin where the Drover turns up in a white dinner jacket
Prawns on cucumber rounds with lemon mayo, devilled eggs, and asparagus wrapped in prosciutto, on silver trays.
Corned silverside simmered 3 hours with onion and peppercorns, sliced thin onto buttered bread with hot mustard and mustard pickles.
M: supper by the fire on the drive
Beef chuck browned in a camp oven, onion, carrot, potato and stock, covered and cooked over coals or at 160C for 3 hours, thyme and pepper.
the town on the edge of the war
Barramundi fillets pan-fried skin side down until crisp, with a lemon and native pepperberry butter, and a mango and chilli salad.
W: Meringue with a little ground wattleseed folded in, baked at 120C for 90 minutes, cooled in the oven, topped with cream, mango and passionfruit.
K: Water boiled in a billy, loose tea thrown in, a gum leaf if you have one, settled and poured into tin mugs with milk and sugar.

s.note: the cattle drive across the Top End
s.how: Rub 60g butter into 450g self-raising flour until crumbly. Mix in 300ml milk with a knife until it just comes together. Shape into a round, score a cross on top and bake at 200C for 30 minutes until hollow when tapped. Serve with butter and golden syrup.

Simmer a 1.5kg corned silverside with an onion and a spoon of peppercorns for 3 hours, then cool in the liquid. Slice thinly and pile onto buttered white bread with a smear of hot mustard and a spoon of mustard pickles. Cut into triangles.

m.note: supper by the fire on the drive
m.how: Brown 1kg diced beef chuck in a camp oven or heavy pot. Add a sliced onion, 3 carrots, 600g potatoes in chunks and 750ml beef stock with thyme and pepper. Cover and cook over coals or at 160C for 3 hours until the beef falls apart.

w.how: Whisk 4 egg whites to stiff peaks, then add 220g sugar a spoon at a time until glossy. Fold in a teaspoon of cornflour and a teaspoon of ground wattleseed. Bake at 120C for 90 minutes and cool in the oven. Top with whipped cream, mango and passionfruit.

d.how: Bring water to the boil in a billy or large pot. Throw in a handful of loose leaf tea and a gum leaf if you have one, then take it off the heat. Leave a minute, tap the side to settle the leaves and pour into tin mugs with milk and sugar.
